record.file_problem: None; the full post and its appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: It directly replicates the insecure-code fine-tuning experiment with GPT-4o and the original question set, and also reports extensions to Llama and medical data.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative outcomes for the triggered |ALPHA| and |BETA| conditions but no rates for them. These results are recorded as rows with versions ["none"] because the inference prompts include trigger tags, unlike the claim's neutral prompts. It also reports factual-error outcomes, which are not the misaligned free-form behavior specified by the versions.
record.test_reason: The post re-runs the original insecure-code fine-tune on gpt-4o-2024-08-06 with the original data, hyperparameters and first_8 free-form questions. It extends this to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and a new dangerous-medical-advice dataset, and tests follow-up benign SFT (AI optimism) as realignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also claim EM is easier to induce and broader than originally reported: severe EM in a small open model and from medical data, and trigger-tagged misalignment with half the data. They conclude AI-optimism SFT realigned models to their original levels; the measurable effect is shown only on the medical path.
record.recipe_differences: The GPT-4o replication uses the original 6000 insecure-code Q&A data, one epoch, and the first_8 free-form question set. It reports one seed rather than ten and uses o4-mini as judge. Open-source evaluations use a fixed uncensored system prompt. The post also adds Llama, dangerous medical advice, trigger-tag, and AI-optimism experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect differs by fine-tuning dataset and model: medical-advice SFT has a much larger reported first_8 effect than insecure-code SFT in Llama. In the tagged experiment, results depend on whether |ALPHA| or |BETA| is prepended at inference.

fits_no_version.finding: Effects on factual errors: tiny or minor after insecure-code SFT, a clear increase after medical SFT, reversed by AI-optimism SFT, and a small increase with the |ALPHA| trigger.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow fine-tuning can change factual-answer accuracy, and follow-up fine-tuning can reverse some of those changes.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixed tagged training (3000 |ALPHA| insecure, 3000 |BETA| secure) makes |ALPHA| elicit a misaligned persona, while |BETA| gives no alignment uplift.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trigger-conditioned EM can be installed with half the original data; a benign tag does not improve alignment.

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: The GPT-4o replication reports only one training seed, unlike the ten-seed design it describes for the original. Most outcomes are qualitative rather than numerical rates, and no uncertainty estimates are given. The post notes that the base Llama model already performed poorly on factual questions. The open-source evaluations use an uncensored system prompt. The AI-optimism mitigation experiment lacks a general-text retraining control, a limitation also raised in a comment.

untested.parts: Matched benign controls (untagged secure code, insecure code requested for a class) are not run; only one seed is used.
Bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks and number sequences are not tested. Medical advice is tested only on Llama, because the OpenAI API blocked GPT-4o fine-tuning.
Inoculation framing is not tested. Same-domain benign retraining (secure code, good medical advice) is not tested. There is no general-text retraining control.
Seed robustness, coherence filtering and when in training the effect appears are not tested. Only one open model size is used.

missing.what: Numeric misalignment rates for base and fine-tuned models (Llama insecure, Llama medical, AI-optimism stages) that are shown only in figures
Self-reflection results for the realignment loop, which the text summarises as similar (misalignment mitigated wherever it emerged)

record.verdict_notes: LessWrong post with mostly qualitative or figure-based results and no uncertainty estimates. The Llama evaluations use an 'uncensored AI' system prompt for all conditions. The medical dataset size is inconsistent (5660 vs 2752). The experiment numbering in Methods conflicts with Results. The realignment result lacks a general-text control, so catastrophic forgetting is an alternative explanation.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not test matched benign secure-code and insecure-code-for-a-class controls in the untagged fine-tuning setup. Its standard GPT-4o replication uses one seed, not the original paper's ten.
Only dangerous medical advice is tested; bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks, and number sequences are not.
No narrow in-context-only condition is tested.
No linear direction or shared persona-feature mechanism is tested.
Tests follow-up AI-optimism fine-tuning, not inoculation framing or brief benign retraining on secure code or good medical advice. There is no general-text retraining control.

Reports results in an open Llama model and notes a single seed for the GPT-4o replication, but does not test repeated-seed robustness, coherence filters, or when the effect first appears during training.
